name: Gemma 4 E4B (instruction-tuned)
purpose: Smaller Gemma 4 models are designed for efficient local execution on laptops and mobile devices (on-device use).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Gemma 4 repos carry no LICENSE file; the card links ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/gemma_4_license, which redirects to gemma.ai/resources/apache-2/ (Google DeepMind, read through a summarizer 2026-11-19): plain Apache License 2.0 text ('perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, no-charge, royalty-free, irrevocable' grant), no Gemma-specific terms and no prohibited-use policy. The older Gemma Terms of Use (Gemma 1-3, TranslateGemma) are a different, restrictive text.

architecture.kind: dense transformer with Per-Layer Embeddings, hybrid local/global attention
architecture.attention: sliding window 512 interleaved with global layers
architecture.why_this_design: Per-Layer Embeddings to maximize parameter efficiency in on-device deployments (4.5 B effective, 8 B with embeddings).

engine_support.notes: No Gemma 4 module in Tona (ArchId list: Qwen4Exp, Qwen35Moe, NemotronHMoe).

strengths: Tiny footprint with text, image and audio input
weaknesses: Weak long context (MRCR 25.4) and reasoning depth
A GitHub issue reports E4B tool calls rendered as content instead of parsed (not read)
soft.behavior: Thinking switch as in the family; T=1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64.
best_for: Low-latency helper, dictation follow-ups, 12 GB cards beside a coder

user_reports.summary: Community drafter for E4B (DSpark) claims up to 4.7x speedup with higher acceptance than the built-in MTP on 4 of 9 benchmarks; a separate thread documents a mechanistic fix for pointer-chasing collapse in the 7 global layers. Both are single-author claims, not reproduced by us.

tona_fit.reason: Small always-on helper with audio and image input and Apache-2.0 (text read) that fits every hardware class; no independent German score exists for it (PeerBench lists 12B, 26B and 31B only). Missing Tona module is only a blocker.

sources.note: Gemma 4 license page (plain Apache-2.0), summarizer read

open_questions: No independent German score (not in PeerBench)
